mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the periods following two consecutive quarters of declining GDPC1.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in the last month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail and food services sales by more than 2% over the last month, combined with an increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3%, signals a significant weakening in consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decrease > 2% and UNRATE increase > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where RSAFS decreased by more than 2% and UNRATE increased by more than 0.3% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4% and the consumer price index increases by more than 0.5% in the last month, it indicates an inflationary environment with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary environment with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where FEDFUNDS is above 4% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 200,000 over the last two months signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the periods following two consecutive months of PAYEMS increasing by more than 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts by more than 10% over the last two months, combined with a decrease in retail and food services sales by more than 1%, signals a significant weakening in demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decrease > 10% and RSAFS decrease > 1% in 2 months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where HOUST decreased by more than 10% and RSAFS decreased by more than 1% within the last two months.
